what: Delta Air Lines is one of the largest airlines in the world, carrying over 200 million passengers a year. A large share of its profit comes not from economy seats but from premium cabins, its loyalty programme and the American Express partnership.
customers: Leisure and business travellers, corporate accounts, cargo shippers and American Express cardholders.
money: ticket revenue, skewed toward premium cabins
payments from American Express for miles, plus cargo and maintenance services
moat: Hub positions at Atlanta, Detroit and Minneapolis where it faces little competition, plus a loyalty programme and card partnership that earn money regardless of seat prices.
risks: Airlines are cyclical and fixed costs are high
Debt of about $18 billion remains from the pandemic years
Pilot and staff contracts have raised labour costs
opportunities: Premium and loyalty revenue grow faster than economy fares and are more stable
American Express payments provide billions of high-margin revenue a year
Limited new aircraft deliveries industry-wide keep capacity growth in check
watch: Premium revenue growth against main cabin, and American Express remuneration.
